theme: 3 terms on values that might be missing

terms.definition: The keyword that means a value is missing, so there is nothing stored there at all.
terms.example: The profile photo is nil until the user picks one from their library.
terms.code:
var photo: String? = "me.png"
photo = nil  // Nothing is stored now.
print(photo == nil)

terms.definition: A type that either holds a value or holds nothing, written with a question mark after the type name.
terms.example: I made the middle name an optional because not every user has one.
terms.code:
// A String, or nothing
var nick: String? = nil
nick = "Rose"
print(nick ?? "No nickname")

terms.definition: A safe way to check whether an optional has a value and, if it does, use that value as a normal constant.
terms.example: Use optional binding to unwrap the email instead of force unwrapping it and risking a crash.

quizzes.question: Which technique uses if let to safely check for a value and then use it as a normal constant?

Today's terms
nil - The keyword that means a value is missing, so there is nothing stored there at all.
Optional - A type that either holds a value or holds nothing, written with a question mark after the type name.
Optional Binding - A safe way to check whether an optional has a value and, if it does, use that value as a normal constant.

facebook.caption:
Hi again, ready for some Swift English? 👋

Today's 3 words:
• nil: the keyword for "no value". Nothing is stored there at all.
• Optional: a type that holds a value or holds nothing. You write it with a question mark.
• Optional Binding: a safe way to check for a value and then use it, without risking a crash.

Every example is read twice, first at normal speed and then slowly, so you can say it out loud with me. Try the quiz at the end and share your answers in the comments!

dialogue.title: Bug report: the app crashes on a new profile
dialogue.setting: Slack huddle about a crash report

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, a user reports a crash on the profile screen. It happens for new accounts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New accounts have no photo yet. I think the photo is nil there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, I see it. The code reads the photo like it always exists.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the photo should be an optional. Then the type says it can be empty.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. I will write String with a question mark. Now it is an optional.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. An optional is either a value or nil, so Swift makes us handle both.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Now Xcode shows an error on the image line. What do I do?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do not use the exclamation mark. That is force unwrapping, and it crashes when the value is nil.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm, but it works on my phone. My account has a photo.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That is the trap. It works until the first user with nil opens the screen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay, okay. So what is the safe way?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use optional binding. You write if let photo, and the code runs only when there is a value.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So optional binding unwraps the photo into a normal constant inside the braces.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. And in the else branch, show a gray placeholder.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. I will use optional binding in the name label too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The middle name is also an optional, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Many users have no middle name, so it is nil.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Perfect. Please push the fix, and I will review it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Done. An optional, nil, and optional binding. Crash fixed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why does the photo not show?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is nil until the user picks one.
